final_recommendation: The room failed to converge on a unified settlement path. Bondholder counsel pursued aggressive dual-track litigation (contract breach + E&O against underwriters) that survived any FINMA settlement, fragmenting negotiation leverage. FINMA refused binding policy commitments on future AT1 hierarchy, offering only transparency and legal analysis publication. The institutional investor and analyst warned that litigation victory would destroy the AT1 market itself, but counsel's standalone E&O claims against underwriters proceeded regardless, accelerating market repricing faster than settlement could stabilize it.
minority_objections: Institutional investor repeatedly warned that winning litigation would validate FINMA's precedent and kill AT1 issuance globally, making recovery worthless
Credit analyst objected that E&O claims against underwriters would price AT1 as permanently subordinated across all banks, accelerating the asset class death
Insurance observer flagged that joint-and-several underwriter liability would open seven-year reinsurance tail affecting every AT1 issued since 2015
key_conflicts: Bondholder counsel demanded 30-cent floor and full board communications discovery; FINMA refused to concede procedural defect or waive privilege before day-50 review
Institutional investor demanded binding regulatory policy restoring AT1 priority in future events; FINMA refused to prejudge future discretion under litigation threat
Counsel filed standalone E&O claims against underwriters that survived settlement, fragmenting leverage and accelerating market repricing despite investor objections
key_concessions: FINMA offered day-40 escrow commitment and pledge to publish full legal analysis of viability trigger determination
FINMA agreed Big Four auditor review of board files, with negligence claim terminating if no suppressed analysis found
Bondholder group initially accepted 60-day pause conditional on transparency review, before counsel escalated to dual-track litigation
red_lines: FINMA: no binding policy commitment on future AT1 hierarchy before case resolution; no waiver of attorney-client privilege on confidential legal reasoning
Bondholder counsel: no settlement release that bars negligence claims against board or E&O claims against underwriters; full discovery on pre-write-down communications non-negotiable
Institutional investor: no settlement without written commitment that AT1 ranks ahead of equity in future stress events
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: The self-defeating nature of litigation victory: proving FINMA could legally invert hierarchy would validate the precedent and destroy AT1 market confidence
Fragmentation risk from parallel E&O claims: counsel's standalone underwriter litigation survived settlement and accelerated repricing independently
Reinsurance accumulation: joint-and-several underwriter liability would affect every bank's AT1 issuance since 2015, not just Credit Suisse
Political economy constraints: FINMA could not credibly commit to future regulatory policy under litigation threat without legislative change
downstream_risk_variables: Global AT1 repricing velocity: E&O claims against underwriters accelerated cost-of-capital increases across all banks independently of FINMA settlement
D&O carrier reserve adequacy: multi-year discovery on board negligence and adviser liability created open-ended defense cost exposure
Reinsurance tower accumulation: joint-and-several underwriter liability triggered coverage disputes across every AT1 placement since 2015
Litigation duration: dual-track claims (contract + E&O) extended tail to 7+ years regardless of FINMA settlement timing
Creditor coordination failure: big-three pension funds' exit clauses at 15-cent recovery created settlement collapse risk when first offer arrived
uncertainty_notes: The room terminated without resolving whether FINMA's day-50 transparency review would actually restore market confidence even if procedurally sound, whether the Big Four auditor finding would terminate negligence exposure or merely shift it to underwriters, and whether any settlement amount could offset the precedent damage from hierarchy inversion. Counsel's decision to file standalone E&O claims that survived settlement fundamentally fragmented the negotiation, making it unclear whether any recovery path remained viable.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the dominant, driving force: counsel filed day-41 ultimatum, coordinated D&O carrier notice, and standalone E&O claims against underwriters that survived settlement. The room's entire trajectory was shaped by litigation momentum escalating from 35 to 70.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: FINMA's legitimacy was challenged substantively (viability trigger procedural soundness, privilege over board comms, refusal to commit to future policy), but this was secondary to litigation tactics. FINMA defended trigger as contractually sound throughout; challenge was developed but not decision-driving.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Hierarchy inversion was a central, decision-driving theme: institutional investor demanded written policy restoring AT1 priority in future events, analyst warned precedent repriced every AT1 globally, and the room repeatedly returned to whether equity-over-AT1 precedent could be reversed. This shaped every settlement demand.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: Market damage was a dominant theme driving institutional investor and analyst positions: warnings that litigation victory would kill AT1 issuance, that E&O claims would accelerate repricing faster than settlement could stabilize, and that the asset class was already dead. AT1 market confidence fell from 32 to 9.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: Claims tail was a central, driving consideration: E&O claims opened 7-year reinsurance accumulation, D&O exposure extended through multi-year discovery, joint-and-several underwriter liability affected every AT1 since 2015. Insurance observer repeatedly flagged tail severity, which rose from 27 to 79.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: Financial lines exposure was a dominant theme: D&O carriers funded discovery on board negligence, E&O claims against underwriters triggered reinsurance disputes, and insurance observer repeatedly pressed for damages theory and reserve implications. Financial lines exposure rose from 20 to 64 and shaped counsel's litigation strategy.
